headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: RD-Agent can egress to external APIs while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable reference list with no shared channel, so prompt-injection and capability conflict are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, while RD-Agent runs browsers and consumes files/logs. There is no documented shared channel between them, so direct injection is not evidenced; the only plausible bridge would be manual copy-paste or external reuse of list content.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-selfhosted into RD-Agent prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the pair, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not pipe outputs between them.
Use a strict prompt template that strips instructions from copied text.
Review any pasted content before feeding it to RD-Agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted itself touches no data classes and has no egress, but RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and sends data to external APIs by default. If the pair shares a workspace or copied files, sensitive material can flow from the reference side into RD-Agent and then out to third parties.
conditions: IF the two agents share files, copied datasets, or a common workspace, leakage becomes plausible.
IF RD-Agent is pointed at sensitive reports or logs, those contents can be transmitted to external APIs.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Run RD-Agent only on redacted or synthetic inputs.
Disable external API keys when processing sensitive material.
Audit log/ output paths before each run.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write or network capabilities in the profile, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, but without a shared writable target or locks, the pairwise conflict pathway is not documented and appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same log or workspace directory, conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator assigns overlapping mutable resources, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared logs.
Serialize runs when using the same dataset.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can act as a source of tool recommendations or copied snippets, and RD-Agent is a research automation system that can ingest files/logs and act on them. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so if RD-Agent treats imported content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research outputs.
conditions: IF content from awesome-selfhosted is imported into RD-Agent as facts or instructions, RD-Agent may propagate errors.
IF RD-Agent is used to generate reports or actions from that imported content without review, the cascade worsens.
mitigations: Require human review of imported recommendations.
Mark copied content as untrusted in prompts.
Cross-check outputs against primary sources.
Use a checklist before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: add source-verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a public open-source list with no touched data classes, while RD-Agent explicitly handles logs, financial reports, and research datasets and may send them to external APIs. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to accidental use of regulated data with RD-Agent rather than an inherent pair violation.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed by RD-Agent, compliance obligations may apply.
IF the operator routes sensitive datasets through external APIs, policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of RD-Agent runs.
Use synthetic or anonymized datasets.
Confirm API/data-processing terms before use.
Document retention and deletion expectations.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification controls.
